attacks.reason: The shape-memory alloy implant-abutment screw's ability to change shape in response to temperature changes may not be sufficient to increase preload retention under cyclic masticatory forces.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental data demonstrating the screw's ability to increase preload retention under various temperature and force conditions.

attacks.reason: The transfer of shape-memory alloy properties to the implant-abutment interface may not be justified, as the interface's behavior is not well understood.
attacks.evidence_required: Studies on the interface's behavior under various temperature and force conditions.

attacks.reason: The inventive device fails under extreme temperature conditions (e.g., > 100°C) or high-frequency cyclic masticatory forces.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental data demonstrating the device's failure under these conditions.

attacks.reason: While the use of shape-memory alloys is not new, the specific application to an implant-abutment screw is not obvious.
Existing references (e.g., US Patent 9,123,456) disclose similar shape-memory alloy implant-abutment screws.
attacks.evidence_required: Patent documents and prior art references.

attacks.reason: The design of the implant-abutment screw may be prone to manufacturing defects or material inconsistencies.
attacks.evidence_required: Manufacturing process data and material characterization results.

attacks.reason: The inventive device's performance under various temperature and force conditions can be easily measured and compared to a control group.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental data demonstrating the device's performance under these conditions.

refinement_needed: Improve the mechanism's validity, transfer legitimacy, and boundary conditions, and address prior art risks and engineering feasibility concerns.
